newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee up vs spot, forward dlr on SBI remark.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee up vs spot, forward dlr on SBI remark.

text.p: The Indian rupee edged up against the dollar in the spot and forward markets on Monday after the chairman of the State Bank of India (SBI) said he expected the rupee to remain stable in the near term, dealers said.

"Premia (on forward dollars) came down after the report," said a dealer, referring to SBI chairman P.G. Kakodkar's Monday interview with Reuters. August dollars fell to 1.27/1.30 rupees from the opening level of 1.28/1.31 rupees, dealers said.
"I personally think the rupee would remain at current levels over the next two to three months," Kakodkar said.
"Sometime ago, the premia rose after he (Kakodkar) said long-term interest rates would continue firm," the dealer said.
The spot dollar moved to 35.89/90 rupees in mid-morning trade compared to the opening level of 35.92/93, he said.
SBI is the leading player in the Indian foreign exchange market.
